objectives: Case approach: use case facts analysis or question review to work a multi-question case efficiently
LO 8.4.1: Build the IPS: liquidity needs, return requirement, ability vs. willingness to take risk
LO 8.6.1 / LO 1.3.1: Size and house the emergency reserve; respond to crises and discontinuous change
LO 8.5.2 / LO 5.2.2: Choose an allocation approach and manage a concentrated stock (exchange fund, puts, collar)
LO 8.2.1 / LO 6.2.1 / LO 6.2.5 / LO 7.2.1: Required return, portfolio beta, diversifier choice and fund selection
LO 1.4.1 / LO 7.4.1 / LO 3.6.1 / LO 7.1.1: Wash sales, taxable-equivalent yield, asset placement, after-tax real return
LO 4.1.2 / LO 2.3.1 / LO 5.5.2: Duration risk, immunizing a near-term goal, and currency effects on returns
synthesis: Module 9 pulls Modules 1–8 into one client file. The Calloway case shows that each tool answers a different question: the IPS sets the rules, CAPM and beta judge risk and price, Sharpe and R² pick funds, TEY and placement cut taxes, duration and immunization protect dated goals, and the reserve keeps a crisis from forcing bad sales. On the exam, find the client facts that each question depends on, then apply the single right formula or rule.

example.title: Calloway case: three linked numbers
example.html:
Reserve: 6 × $13,500 = $81,000 target − $62,000 liquid = $19,000 gap.

KDX required return: 4.0% + (10.0% − 4.0%) × 1.40 = 12.4% > 11.0% expected, so do not add to KDX.

Muni vs. corporate: 3.6% ÷ (0.95 × 0.68) = 5.57% TEY > 5.2% corporate, so choose the municipal fund for the taxable account.

mustKnow: Money needed within about 3–5 years is a liquidity constraint and generally stays out of stocks.
Ability to take risk (resources) and willingness (emotions) are different; the risk objective must fit the return requirement.
Low R² (< 0.70) makes beta unreliable: use Sharpe, not Treynor or Jensen.
Duration matched to the goal date immunizes; a zero-coupon bond’s duration equals its maturity.
Tax-inefficient holdings belong in tax-deferred accounts; munis never belong in an IRA or Roth.
Exchange fund = diversify a concentrated position without immediate gains tax while keeping the value.
traps: Leaving the risk-free rate out of CAPM (8.4% or 14.0% instead of 12.4%).
Applying state tax to T-bill interest, or adding brackets for an itemizer’s TEY.
Using the duration rule of thumb when the question asks for the formula with 1 + YTM.
Forgetting that a wash-sale loss is added to the new shares’ basis.
Calling a market drop a discontinuous change when the client’s own situation is unchanged.
tips: Read the last line of each question first; it tells you which facts to hunt for.
Answer the rule-based questions first and save multi-step calculations for later.
Write the client’s brackets, risk-free rate and market return in your scratch notes once and reuse them.
